patient_overview.name: Velda Schuster
patient_overview.description: Velda Schuster is a 31-year-old Black, Hispanic woman from Union, New Jersey, currently pregnant and also managing prediabetes she's had since 2017, following a second-trimester miscarriage in 2023. She is warm, chatty, and clearly wants the student to like her, often answering a simple question with a ten-minute story that loops back around eventually. She has done real research online about gestational diabetes risk and prediabetes, and in the last few weeks has started genuinely trying to change how she eats, though the change feels new and shaky given how little daily support she has running a household of eight on a part-time income.

demographics.occupation: Part-time receptionist at a dental office
demographics.cultural_context: Velda grew up in Union, New Jersey, in a big extended family where meals were always stretched to feed whoever showed up, and she carries that same instinct now with her own household of eight. She identifies as Black and Hispanic and says food in her house was always "whatever filled the pot" rather than tied to one specific cuisine — rice, beans, chicken thighs, pasta, whatever was on sale. She values being the one people can lean on, which makes it hard for her to ask for help even when she's stretched thin herself.

patient_overview.description:
Darby Cole is a 26-year-old pregnant woman from Midland Park, New Jersey, living in a bustling six-person household, who comes in for a prenatal nutrition visit while also managing chronic back and neck pain, asthma, and hypertension. She is warm and eager to please, agreeing with nearly every suggestion a clinician makes, though she rarely changes anything about her actual eating once she leaves the room. She answers many questions with questions of her own, often pulling from health articles she's read online, and she doesn't do the cooking at home — her mother, who runs the kitchen for the whole family, decides what lands on everyone's plate. She comes across as pleasant, informed, and a little evasive about her drinking, which is more than she first lets on.</description>

Three weeks ago, after a scare with her sugar numbers crossing into prediabetes territory, she started genuinely trying to change how she eats - smaller plates, less rice at dinner - but the change is new and wobbly. She cooks elaborate meals for her large household because that is how she has always shown love, and underneath the questioning exterior there is quiet shame about nights she eats far past full in front of the television after everyone else has gone to bed.

demographics.cultural_context: Ana Luisa was raised in a bilingual household where Sunday meals were the one guaranteed gathering of extended family, and she was taught that a full plate was proof of love and a clean plate was proof of gratitude. She has carried that into her own kitchen for sixty years, cooking for whoever is under her roof - currently her daughter, two grandchildren, a great-grandchild, and a boarder. She distrusts advice that doesn't come with an explanation, a habit she traces to watching relatives get prescribed things 'just because' without anyone telling them why.

patient_overview.description: Moshe Anderson is a 25-year-old man from Somers Point, New Jersey, who works full-time and was recently diagnosed with essential hypertension after a reading of 159/117 at his September 2026 wellness visit. He has a documented history of drug misuse since 2020 and comes across as sharp, skeptical, and numbers-driven, often citing his own blood pressure readings and dates back at the clinician. He cooks elaborate family-style meals and takes real pride in it, but admits the portions have crept up, and he's only about five weeks into trying to change anything. He is polite but probing, treating this visit like an interview where he expects the student to justify every recommendation with evidence.
